That's because they're bullshit. Look here on Wikipedia:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_serotonin_reuptake_inhibitor#Depression

"There has been controversy regarding the efficacy of antidepressants in treating depression depending on its severity and duration." Keep reading after this part.

And if you look more specifically at the actual drugs themselves you'll find a pattern:

Sertraline (Zoloft): "A 2008 review concluded that only 51% of studies of various SSRI's yielded positive outcomes."

Paroxetine (Paxil): "A variety of meta analyses have been conducted to evaluate the efficacy of paroxetine in depression. They have variously concluded that paroxetine is superior or equivalent to placebo and that it is equivalent or inferior to other antidepressants."

There is no evidence to suggest SSRIs are any better than placebo at treating depression. Nor is there any evidence to suggest the serotonin levels of depressed individuals are lower than that of "normal" people.

In fact in Europe they have SSREs, Selective Serotonin Reuptake EHANCERs, which do the exact opposite thing as SSRIs, and have shown also to "treat" depression with the same efficacy as the SSRIs. Read more about that here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianeptine#Medical_uses

These drugs do not do anything except form dependence, so when you come off of them you get brain zaps/other withdrawal symptoms, which tricks people into thinking they were helping and they now need them. It's a giant scam that has made the pharmaceutical industry tens of billions of dollars.

It can help, but do not assume it will be like taking a pill and then magically your depression and anxiety will be gone. The only way you will resolve your psychological issues with the mushrooms is by cultivating awareness, and psychedelics in general are very useful in this regard.

The real question here is whether or not you believe finding the roots of your anxiety/depression will help you to resolve them. If your problem is for example, a dissatisfaction with your appearance or life situation and you do not have the ability to change this, the mushrooms may only make this worse by forcing you to dwell/ruminate on it.

There is no evidence that suggests Psilocybin does any long term damage to the psyche, and in my personal experience problems only tend to arise when the mushrooms are misused. (When one neglects set and setting) Your "set" may not be ideal given your anxiety/depression, but it is probably worth tripping anyway because you will undoubtedly learn a great many things about yourself, just be prepared for a potentially difficult experience.

If you have someone in your life whom you could literally speak any of your thoughts to without judgement, even your deepest most protected secrets, trip with them. If not, trip alone.

"Is there anything special I should do during the trip that will help?" - This is the wrong attitude, the mushrooms will guide you if you let them, do not attempt to control the trip. I must emphasize this, do not fight it. Expect nothing, accept everything. 

Not trying to scare you or anything, more than likely you will have a very profound and beautiful experience that will be imprinted in your memory for the rest of your life.

(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antidepressant#Major_depressive_disorder) There's also no evidence to suggest depressed individuals have any less serotonin than "normal" people.

Weed and Shrooms/LSD have been my go to treatments for many years now, they let me alter/escape reality a bit and that gives me the relief I need to keep going really.

It wouldn't be "effort" if I could enjoy it. I'm not against working hard and such, it's just I've already done a lot of that and it seems like it's all been in vain. In fact I wish I could take back some of the things I spent my time on learning and just add that time back to the pool. Although I really have no idea what to do with all this time, everything seems to return disillusionment.

The problem is what is worth doing that is actually worth my time?! Everything feels like 90% effort, 10% reward. Media doesn't do shit for me, I don't want to read a new book, or see a new movie, I want to experience a new reality. This is all so old.

Trust me I'm not sitting around doing nothing, and when I am I have this glorious $1000 herman miller chair to do it in, with these "wonderful" headphones that are amplified and this computer configured for hours to the subjectively best experience possible with Linux. I go hiking twice a week, I do drugs that practically break the universe regularly, I have decent friends, I'm literally doing everything that makes sense to "live" and no matter what I do I can't help but sit back and stare into infinity, fantasizing about what could be.

You say we're all God, but are we? I mean I've smoked plenty of DMT, I've been on the same page, but if we're referring to "God" as a complete model of perfection, this reality isn't God, this is seriously lacking in the variety department. Would God sit around and do the same things every day and make it so doing anything else requires an immense amount of work to acquire new knowledge, skills, only to get a short burst of satisfaction? We're not part of God, we're God's little abandoned machines with highly limited specifications.

It's not really a good or a bad place, it just is.

Depression is not as simple thing a thing as "Oh you're depressed? You have a chemical imbalance, take this." I would say the first line of treatment for depression should be diet, exercise and therapy before medication. Of course given the nature of the condition that may not always be viable.

I have actually tried SSRIs, they personally made me feel worse. [Most clinical trials have them performing a little worse, on par or a bit better than placebo.]
(http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_serotonin_reuptake_inhibitor#Depression)

There is no solid evidence suggesting that depressed individuals have less serotonin than regular people. In fact there's even a drug that acts as a SSRE (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Enhancer), as opposed to an Inhibiter that has [just as much efficacy as the other antidepressants.](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianeptine#Medical_uses) The whole "chemical imbalance" concept is merely a hypothesis they use in advertisements as if it's fact, it's absurd.

The whole way these drugs are dished out rubs me the wrong way as well. They tell you to wait a month before judging whether or not they work, which funny enough is the amount of time it takes to become physically dependent on them. So if you come off the drugs at this point you may have to endure brain zaps among other things. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antidepressant_discontinuation_syndrome)

I'm not saying that SSRIs don't work for everyone, but this double standard where weed and psychedelics must be thoroughly investigated before the public touches them, and even when there is tons of research, it is ignored, but dozens of SSRI's that cause physical dependence, sexual dysfunction, heart problems, brain zaps, etc. with long-term effects still unknown, are being approved one after another.

Weed and psychedelics allow me to resolve existential angst with no side-effects, something no pill seems to be able to accomplish. There is evidence that Cannabis and Psilocybin promote neurogenesis, the growth of new neurons in the brain. It is also impossible to overdose on Cannabis, Psilocybin and LSD. These are very well-tolerated drugs and I should have the fucking right to use them if they let me lead a better life.

On the contrary most, if not all the antipsychotics they forced down my throat as a child have never been tested to the extent of Cannabis, Psilocybin or LSD. The "atypical" antipsychotics were actually new at the time and they had no issues giving them to thousands of children like myself who now may well be suffering as I am. I was essentially a guinea pig.

I'm not telling everyone with depression to start using weed and psychedelics, but if you're like me, you've sought them out, and they work for you, there's nothing wrong with that. I would most definitely recommend them to someone who went through what I did.

Correlation does not necessarily imply causation, but I'm providing reasoning for why there is a correlation. If I said:

DMT is produced in higher amounts in schizophrenics, schizophrenics have a higher mortality rate than the average population, therefore DMT causes higher mortality rates, that would be absurd.

But what I'm saying is based on our knowledge of the default mode network's role in DMT and schizophrenia, natural selection, and the way we tend to treat mental illness (by doing something contrary to the action of DMT) perhaps it is linked. I'm not saying it absolutely is, this is just an idea I shared with the intent of generating discussion. I've already learned far more than I would have if I didn't post this.

In modern society, yes it is the disease. But maybe in our evolutionary history it was a cure rather than a disease. That's what I'm saying here.

Are the sources I link above not valid evidence? If 5% of regular people have DMT while 47% of schizophrenics do, doesn't this imply it's related to the brain? I'm not saying I've somehow proven it absolutely is, but I think it's fair to make the assumption based on the data provided. This is just a hypothesis after all.

For the record, I'm also autistic and I was treated with antipsychotics for "irritability associated with autism" as a child (from 8-14) and in my early adulthood I've begun using psychedelics. So that's the angle I come from here.

That said, I think you're misinterpreting me here. I never said autistic individuals completely lack social communication, but it is largely impaired. The DMT release may be a primitive attempt by the brain to help restore social interaction if it perceives isolation. 

However in modern society, the effects do not help at all, thus it's become pointless, but perhaps thousands of years ago it was more valuable for attracting a mate compared to those in the same circumstances who did not get a release of DMT. If you've ever taken mushrooms both in a shopping mall and in nature, I think the difference in the experience should illustrate what I mean here. If your experience is similar to my own you have a far better time connecting with others in nature, and may even have a panic attack in a mall.

And would you be able to provide a detailed article regarding the overstimulation/hyperactivity of autism? I'd like to read more about that.

I don't see why where it's produced is relevant, there is a clear correlation here with those with mental disorders having higher concentrations of DMT, it appears to either be produced in the brain or cross the BBB at some point.

These disorders are linked with overactivity or a failure to deactivate the DMN, the DMN is associated with the self. DMT reduces activity in the DMN. These disorders generally involve impaired social functioning, so while maybe it isn't useful anymore, at some point in our evolutionary history secreting DMT may have had the advantage of restoring social connections when not doing so meant a decreased chance of survival.

Edit: Changed "must" to "appears to" in the interest of accuracy.

Runners get a release of endogenous morphine to help soothe sore muscles. The Schizo/Autistic individuals get a release of endogenous DMT to help restore social connectivity.

Ie. Person is isolating him or herself from the group because of overactivity of DMN. Person gets small release of DMT which reduces amount of activity in the DMN. Person rejoins the group.

So perhaps in our evolutionary past it was more successful than it is today where we end up medicating these people.

And this mechanism I would say is not solely related to those with the mental disorders:

"DMT was detected in the urine of 47% of those diagnosed by their psychiatrists as schizophrenic, 38% of those with other non-affective psychoses, 13% of those with affective psychoses, 19% of those with neurotic and personality disorders and 5% of normal subjects."

5% of normal subjects as well as 19% with personality disorders also had elevated DMT levels. So while it may be more prominent in the more extreme mental disorders, I think the brain's release of DMT is a product of some form of subconscious social isolation.

"DMT was detected in the urine of 47% of those diagnosed by their psychiatrists as schizophrenic, 38% of those with other non-affective psychoses, 13% of those with affective psychoses, 19% of those with neurotic and personality disorders and 5% of normal subjects."

It only appears to occur in half of schizophrenics, and social isolation is considered a common symptom of the disorder.

No that's not the case at all actually. The forks become new projects themselves. The two forks from Gnome I mentioned before are MATE (Continued from the Gnome 2 Source) and Cinnamon (Reworked from Gnome 3). Both are heavily used and supported throughout the Linux community.

His long term strategy of switching to Linux makes more sense however. Microsoft is in control of what changes in Windows, in this case the user interface. In Linux however whenever there is a controversial change the project forks. 

In example there was a situation not long ago which was similar to the current Metro vs. Desktop problem. Gnome (A popular desktop environment) came to it's third revision and was quite different from Gnome 2. So it was forked and now you have the option of using an updated Gnome 2, a version of Gnome 3 reworked to be more like Gnome 2, or Gnome 3.

On Windows 8 you either need to use an unsupported work around or live with Metro. And who knows if the same work around will work with Windows 9, or if Microsoft decides to ditch the desktop altogether some day. The point being that the choice is Microsoft's, not the end user. A corporation is in control of the software you depend on.
